newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares open bourse higher, boosted by Dow.
newsitem.headline: German shares open bourse higher, boosted by Dow.

text.p: German shares started bourse dealings higher on Wednesday, after Wall Street hit yet another record high, but gains were capped as a jump in a German business climate index undermined rate cut hopes, dealers said.

Had it not been for the rise in the German Ifo index for October, which pulled German bonds and pre-bourse share dealings lower, the DAX index of 30 leading shares could have reached up to record highs above 2,800 points, dealers said.
As it was, the DAX rose 16.04 points, or 0.58 percent, to 2,780.13 points by 1033 GMT.
Earlier, news that October German M3 money supply growth was steady at 8.4 percent had little effect on either bond or share markets.

The morning's most heavily traded stock was Deutsche Telekom, which has led volumes since shares in the national telecommunications giant were first traded on Monday, although volumes were subsiding, dealers said.
Telekom was down 17 pfennigs in early bourse trade to 31.90 marks, as investors continued to take profit.

Shares in steelmaker and diversified industrial group Thyssen AG rose most among DAX stocks, climbing almost six percent or 15.5 marks to 285 marks, after the firm said its supervisory board would decide on Friday on plans to reorganise the group.
Pharmaceutical group Merck KGaA gained ground after its nine month figures came out better than expected. Merck was up 2.05 marks, almost four percent, at 56.80 marks in early bourse dealings.
Shares in specialty chemicals company SKW Trostberg AG and tyre maker Continental AG were both boosted by the companies' respective nine month results.
SKW Trostberg was up 1.60 marks to 43 marks, while Continental rose 1.10 marks to 26.40 marks.
